### Problem: Wildcard matching {#sec-st-p4-wild}

::: {.p-statement}
`?` matches any one character. `*` matches any sequence, including the empty one. Return whether `p` matches the whole of `s`.

$0 \le |s|, |p| \le 2000$. `aa` against `a` is false. `aa` against `*` is true. `cb` against `?a` is false. `adceb` against `*a*b` is true. `acdcb` against `a*c?b` is false.

Source: [LC 44 · Wildcard Matching](https://leetcode.com/problems/wildcard-matching/){.solved difficulty="Hard"}
:::

::: {.p-intuition}
A star that is allowed to be empty and allowed to grow by one character is two arrows, not a search. The first star of `*a*b` on `adceb` is empty, `a` takes the first letter, and the second star takes `dce`. No other split works, because there is only one `a`, but the table does not have to know that in advance.
:::

::: {.p-approach}
- **State.** $dp[i][j]$ = `p[0..j)` matches `s[0..i)`.
- **Transition.** A star reads the cell to the left or the cell above. `?` or an equal letter reads the diagonal.
- **Base.** $dp[0][0]$ is true. A prefix of only stars matches the empty text. **Answer.** $dp[n][m]$.
:::

The buttons are in order. Each one keeps the previous solution and changes only what that form changes.

::: {.panel-tabset .solution-forms}

#### Recursion

::: {.form-next}
`f(i, j)` matches the suffixes. A star tries the empty match and the one-character match. The recursion is the definition, and a pattern of many stars recomputes the same suffixes.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("wild", "rec")
    assert str(final) == "true"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: st-wild-rec
def wild_rec(s, p):
    def f(i, j):
        if j == len(p):
            return i == len(s)
        if p[j] == "*":
            if f(i, j + 1):
                return True
            return i < len(s) and f(i + 1, j)
        if i < len(s) and (p[j] == "?" or p[j] == s[i]):
            return f(i + 1, j + 1)
        return False
    return f(0, 0)
```

##### C++

```cpp
bool wildRec(int i, int j, const string& s, const string& p) {
    if (j == (int)p.size()) return i == (int)s.size();
    if (p[j] == '*') return wildRec(i, j + 1, s, p) || (i < (int)s.size() && wildRec(i + 1, j, s, p));
    if (i < (int)s.size() && (p[j] == '?' || p[j] == s[i])) return wildRec(i + 1, j + 1, s, p);
    return false;
}
```
:::

#### Memo

::: {.form-next}
Store every suffix pair, including the failures. The body does not change.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("wild", "memo")
    assert str(final) == "true"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: st-wild-memo
def wild_memo(s, p):
    memo = {}

    def f(i, j):
        if (i, j) not in memo:
            if j == len(p):
                memo[i, j] = i == len(s)
            elif p[j] == "*":
                memo[i, j] = f(i, j + 1) or (i < len(s) and f(i + 1, j))
            else:
                memo[i, j] = i < len(s) and (p[j] == "?" or p[j] == s[i]) and f(i + 1, j + 1)
        return memo[i, j]

    return f(0, 0)
```

##### C++

```cpp
int wildMemo(int i, int j, const string& s, const string& p, vector<vector<int>>& memo) {
    if (memo[i][j] >= 0) return memo[i][j];
    if (j == (int)p.size()) return memo[i][j] = i == (int)s.size();
    if (p[j] == '*')
        return memo[i][j] = wildMemo(i, j + 1, s, p, memo) || (i < (int)s.size() && wildMemo(i + 1, j, s, p, memo));
    bool ok = i < (int)s.size() && (p[j] == '?' || p[j] == s[i]) && wildMemo(i + 1, j + 1, s, p, memo);
    return memo[i][j] = ok;
}
```
:::

#### Table

::: {.form-next}
Empty pattern matches only empty text. A leading run of stars matches empty text. A star cell is the OR of "use nothing" and "consume one more". Everything else is a diagonal.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("wild", "tab")
    assert str(final) == "true"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: st-wild-tab
def wild_tab(s, p):
    n, m = len(s), len(p)
    dp = [[False] * (m + 1) for _ in range(n + 1)]
    dp[0][0] = True
    for j in range(1, m + 1):
        if p[j - 1] == "*":
            dp[0][j] = dp[0][j - 1]
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        for j in range(1, m + 1):
            if p[j - 1] == "*":
                dp[i][j] = dp[i][j - 1] or dp[i - 1][j]
            elif p[j - 1] == "?" or p[j - 1] == s[i - 1]:
                dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j - 1]
    return dp[n][m]
```

##### C++

```cpp
bool wildTab(const string& s, const string& p) {
    int n = s.size(), m = p.size();
    vector<vector<char>> dp(n + 1, vector<char>(m + 1));
    dp[0][0] = 1;
    for (int j = 1; j <= m; ++j)
        if (p[j - 1] == '*') dp[0][j] = dp[0][j - 1];
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i)
        for (int j = 1; j <= m; ++j) {
            if (p[j - 1] == '*') dp[i][j] = dp[i][j - 1] || dp[i - 1][j];
            else if (p[j - 1] == '?' || p[j - 1] == s[i - 1]) dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j - 1];
        }
    return dp[n][m];
}
```
:::

#### Greedy star

::: {.form-next}
Walk both strings. A letter or `?` that matches advances both. A star records its position and the text index it might grow from. On a later mismatch, resume just after that star and let it consume one more character. Stars at the end of the pattern may be empty. This uses the fact that a wildcard star can absorb anything, which a regex star cannot.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("wild", "star")
    assert str(final) == "true"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: st-wild-star
def wild_greedy(s, p):
    i = j = 0
    star = match = -1
    while i < len(s):
        if j < len(p) and (p[j] == "?" or p[j] == s[i]):
            i += 1
            j += 1
        elif j < len(p) and p[j] == "*":
            star, match = j, i
            j += 1
        elif star != -1:
            match += 1
            i, j = match, star + 1
        else:
            return False
    while j < len(p) and p[j] == "*":
        j += 1
    return j == len(p)

assert wild_rec("aa", "*") is True
assert wild_memo("aa", "a") is False
assert wild_tab("cb", "?a") is False
assert wild_tab("adceb", "*a*b") is True
assert wild_greedy("acdcb", "a*c?b") is False
assert wild_greedy("adceb", "*a*b") is True
assert wild_tab("", "") is True and wild_tab("", "*") is True and wild_tab("a", "") is False
```

##### C++

```cpp
bool wildGreedy(const string& s, const string& p) {
    int i = 0, j = 0, star = -1, match = -1, n = s.size(), m = p.size();
    while (i < n) {
        if (j < m && (p[j] == '?' || p[j] == s[i])) { ++i; ++j; }
        else if (j < m && p[j] == '*') { star = j; match = i; ++j; }
        else if (star != -1) { i = ++match; j = star + 1; }
        else return false;
    }
    while (j < m && p[j] == '*') ++j;
    return j == m;
}
```
:::

:::

::: {.p-complexity}
**Recursion** is exponential in the number of stars. **Memoisation** and the **table** are $O(nm)$. The **greedy** scan is $O(n + m)$: each text index is the resume point of the latest star at most once. $|s|, |p| \le 2000$ allows the table. The greedy is the one to ship, and it is not the regex algorithm.
:::

::: {.p-edge}
- Empty text, empty pattern: true. Empty text, a pattern of only stars: true. Empty pattern, non-empty text: false.
- `*` against any text: true. One star consumes the whole string.
- `?` consumes exactly one character and does not care which.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistakes"}
- A star that cannot be empty. `*` against the empty string is true, and the first star of `*a*b` on `adceb` is empty.
- Using this greedy on `x*`. A regex star absorbs only copies of `x`. The same backtrack answers false on `aab` against `a*b*ab`, which does match.
- Matching a prefix and ignoring the rest of the text. The pattern has to consume `s` exactly.
:::

**Variants.** `*` that may cover at most $k$ characters replaces the unbounded "up" arrow by a loop of length $k$. Counting the ways a star can be split is the same table with sums. Scramble, which cuts and optionally swaps the two sides, is a different recursion on substrings: [LC 87 · Scramble String](https://leetcode.com/problems/scramble-string/){difficulty="Hard"}.
